title: Florida’s $1.8 trillion economy claim is backed by BEA data—but the “14th-largest” ranking can’t be verified from the Chamber release alone
summary: The Florida Chamber Foundation and Fox Business tout Florida as the world’s No. 14 in nominal GDP, using BEA’s official state GDP series as the base; but the article says the Chamber’s specific country-comparison method and calculations aren’t fully reproducible here, and the figure measures size—not resident affordability or welfare.

claims.text: A nominal GDP rank can legitimately indicate an economy’s scale and its ability to attract capital and talent, but it does not by itself establish broad prosperity, affordability, or household well-being.

The strongest counter-reading is that comparing a U.S. state to sovereign countries is a rhetorical device built on nominal-dollar size, and that policy vindication from the rank is incomplete without affordability, real growth, and distributional context.
